comment: Sovereignty should emphasise effective control and substitutability. The statement that countries should not be dependent on actors outside their jurisdiction may be interpreted as requiring technological or hosting self-sufficiency. Elsewhere, the guidance appropriately allows private-sector hosting, regional shared infrastructure, international standards and cross-border federated services.

citation.section: Section 1.4 - Autonomy and Sovereignty, p. 21, lines 412-416.

public.text: Sovereignty should emphasise effective control and substitutability. The statement that countries should not be dependent on actors outside their jurisdiction may be interpreted as requiring technological or hosting self-sufficiency. Elsewhere, the guidance appropriately allows private-sector hosting, regional shared infrastructure, international standards and cross-border federated services.
public.suggestedRevision: Reframe sovereignty in terms of effective governance control, continuity, portability and substitutability rather than absence of external dependency. Explicitly recognise that external or regional providers may be used where countries retain control over critical data and governance, maintain viable exit/transition arrangements, and can continue essential functions without unacceptable vendor or jurisdictional lock-in.
